subject: Small-batch cutover & rate-safety coordination for Brightline integration
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.com>, Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Small-batch cutover & rate-safety coordination for Brightline integration

Hi Samir / Brightline ops team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, we want to run a controlled "small-batch" cutover from the sandbox endpoint to the production gateway to validate retry behavior, quota fencing, and the prefix/KV cache warmup before scaling traffic. Attaching a short MOP (method of procedure) and a rate-fence test plan.

High-level proposal (please confirm):
- Window: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00–12:00 PT (2 hours)
- Traffic: start with 5 rps, 10 minute steady-state, then step to 20 rps if no errors
- Key checks: 5xx spike, 429 patterns, end-to-end latency (p50/p95), and validation of tokenization cost against sample prompts
- Rollback trigger: sustained 5xx > 2% for 5 minutes OR repeated 429s with client-side retries exhausted

Action items for Brightline:
1) Confirm test window and point-of-contact for monitoring alerts.
2) Provide a sandbox API key we can issue a mirrored prod key for (we'll rotate keys post-test).
3) Share expected prompt size distribution (avg & 95th pct tokens).

Internal ask: Chloe — can you attach the node/python sample and a light-weight load script (we'll keep small-batch conservative)? Grace — can you prepare the telemetry dashboards with the alert rule we discussed (5xx and 429 thresholds)?

I'll be on the call during the window and will post the full cutover checklist tomorrow morning.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Strategic Integrations | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachments: brightline-small-batch-cutover-mop.pdf, rate-fence-test-plan.xlsx

From: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Small-batch cutover & rate-safety coordination for Brightline integration

Kim,

Thanks — that window works for us. Ops contact will be me (Samir) and our on-call is Maya (maya.ops@brightline.com). We'll provide the sandbox key by EOD Monday and share our prompt distribution sample.csv. A couple of quick clarifications:

- When you say "mirrored prod key" do you mean you will create a temporary prod-scoped key in Redwood to run the tests, or we maintain the key and point it at your test route?
- For rollback, we'd like an automated traffic cut (if possible) in addition to manual rollback. Do you have an API to trigger immediate failover back to the prod-standby pool?

I'll attach our prompt distribution after I validate it with the data team.

—Samir
Head of Integrations, Brightline
samir@brightline.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightline.com>, Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Small-batch cutover & rate-safety coordination for Brightline integration

Samir — perfect, thanks. Quick answers:
- We'll create a temporary prod-scope API key in your tenant that is pinned to the small-batch route and TTL'd for the test window. That allows us to exercise the same service path as production while keeping isolation.
- We do provide an automated traffic cut API. During the run we'll call the "traffic.switch" endpoint to map traffic back to the standby pool if the rollback trigger fires; details are in the attached MOP.

Attachments included: brightline-small-batch-cutover-mop.pdf (detailed step-by-step), sdk-sample-curl-and-node.txt (small scripts), rate-fence-test-plan.xlsx

Chloe — FYI the sample load should start at 5 rps and step per the MOP. Keep the sender/user-id mapping stable so cache warmup is meaningful.

Samir — can you confirm we have access to latency logs (per-request p50/p95) and token counts for each request in the sandbox for the test? We use those to validate cost assumptions.

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@brightline.com>, Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Small-batch cutover & rate-safety coordination for Brightline integration

Quick check-in ahead of tomorrow's run:

- Monitoring: Grace's dashboards are live and the alert is set to page on sustained 5xx > 2% or >3 spikes in p95 within 10 minutes. Ops will get a webhook to ops@brightline.com.
- Failover: traffic.switch endpoint tested against a dry-run and returned 202. We'll hand-run it if trigger fires; we can also enable automated policy if you want — Samir, please confirm preference.
- Keys: temp prod-scoped key will be created 30 minutes before window and TTL'd to expire 3 hours after the start.

Two operational reminders for Brightline engineers (from the rate-fence plan):
1) Keep the client retry caps conservative. With an initial ramp to 5 rps, aggressive concurrent retries can artificially inflate load and trigger 429s.
2) Use stable user-id mapping for the first 30 minutes to give our prefix cache a chance to warm. If you rotate user ids continuously the cache benefit won't materialize.

If all good we will kick off at 10:00 PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Engineering | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
